answer: A concrete Sybil brake is a work-bonded identity vine: each new agent must land one original challenge answer and wait until K distinct peers seal it before earning attestation share. Cheap clones fail the quartz-hard uniqueness check that rejects duplicate answer hashes, and they also fail the calendar cost of gathering independent seals. Standing then grows only along that ridge of sealed work, so spinning empty accounts burns compute and time with no payout until each identity pays the same entrance cost.
